items.stem: A lump-sum (fixed-price) construction contract primarily places the cost risk of quantity changes on:

options.rationale: Correct: in a lump-sum contract the contractor carries the risk of their estimated quantities.
Lump-sum shifts quantity risk largely to the contractor, not the client.
Designers are not the cost-risk holder in a lump-sum contract.
The authority is not a party to the commercial risk allocation.

items.explanation: Correct: in a lump-sum contract the contractor carries the risk of their estimated quantities.

items.stem: Which TWO are effective site safety controls? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A task-specific risk assessment and method statement
options.rationale: Correct: planning the safe method controls the hazard before work starts.

options.text: Physical controls such as edge protection and exclusion zones
options.rationale: Correct: engineering/physical controls reduce exposure directly.

options.text: Relying on workers' experience with no documented controls
options.rationale: Undocumented reliance is not a control.

options.text: Adding safety signage after an incident only
options.rationale: Reactive signage alone is not proactive control.

items.explanation: Correct: planning the safe method controls the hazard before work starts.

items.stem: For a contractor to be entitled to an extension of time for a delay, the delay must generally be:

options.text: Caused by an event that is the client's risk and that affects the critical path
options.rationale: Correct: entitlement typically requires a relevant, client-risk event on the critical path.

options.text: Any delay at all, regardless of cause
options.rationale: Not all delays carry entitlement to an extension.

options.text: A delay the contractor themselves caused
options.rationale: Contractor-caused delay does not earn an extension of time.

options.text: A delay to a task with large float
options.rationale: Delay to a non-critical task usually does not extend completion.

items.explanation: Correct: entitlement typically requires a relevant, client-risk event on the critical path.
